title: $(2, 2k)$-hypercontractivity for the noise operator
statement:
Fix an integer $k \ge 1$ and a real number $\rho$ with $\rho^2 \le \dfrac{1}{2k-1}$.
Then for every function $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ on the Boolean hypercube,
\[
  \E\bigl[(T_\rho f)^{2k}\bigr] \;\le\; \bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^{k},
\]
where the expectation is taken under the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$ and $T_\rho$ is
the noise operator $T_\rho f = \sum_{S \subseteq [n]} \rho^{|S|}\,\hat f(S)\,\chi_S$.
Equivalently, $\norm{T_\rho f}_{2k} \le \norm{f}_2$.
hypotheses_covered: k is a positive integer (1 ≤ k)
f is a Boolean function {0,1}^n → ℝ
replaced:
For any Boolean function $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$, integer $k \ge 1$, and noise
parameter $\rho$ with $\rho^2 \le 1/(2k-1)$,
\[
  \E[(T_\rho f)^{2k}] \le \bigl(\E[f^2]\bigr)^k,
\]
equivalently $\norm{T_\rho f}_{2k} \le \norm{f}_2$.
